headline: Ukraine is reported to be planning a bigger campaign of AI-guided drones to disrupt flights at Moscow's airports.
score_reason: Strong robotics-in-war angle with real effects on flights, but a plan reported second-hand and not yet authorised.
importance_line: Air travellers around Moscow are already hit by cancellations, and a larger AI-drone campaign would raise the stakes for civilian aviation, but President Zelenskyy has not approved the aggressive version.
summary: The Atlantic reports, as relayed by UNITED24 Media, that Ukraine is preparing a larger AI-powered drone campaign to disrupt Russian air traffic, after Moscow airports cancelled 345 flights in the week before 15 Oct 2026. The original proposal envisioned up to 1,000 drones a day using map-matching navigation to cope with Russian jamming, but President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not authorised the more aggressive version because of civilian safety concerns.
notes: Source chain: The Atlantic, read as relayed by UNITED24 Media (link is the UNITED24 page). Military story: counts toward the robot-war limit.
